Theorem family
<corollary> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <corollary> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the corollary’s label, parallel to Theorem 1. ‘s name kwarg.
+numbered boolean default true Whether this corollary participates in the propositional theorem-family shared counter. Default true.

Produced by: canonical <corollary>.

 Examples <corollary | Every prime greater than 2 is odd.> <corollary #cor:bounded> Any continuous function on a closed interval is bounded. </corollary>
<definition> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <definition> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the definition’s label.
+numbered boolean default true Whether this definition participates in the definition counter. Definition 1. runs on its own counter (separate from the propositional theorem-family counter), matching amsthm’s conventional “definition” theorem-style family. Default true.

Produced by: canonical <definition>.

 Examples <definition | A *group* is a set with an associative binary operation, identity, and inverses.> <definition name="Group" #def:group> A *group* is a set $G$ together with a binary operation $\cdot$ satisfying associativity, identity, and inverses. </definition>
<example> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <example> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the example’s label.
+numbered boolean default true Whether this example participates in the example counter. Example 1. runs on its own counter (separate from theorem, lemma, definition counters), matching amsthm’s conventional “example” theorem-style family. Default true.

Produced by: canonical <example>.

 Examples <example | The integers under addition form a group.> <example #ex:integers> The integers $\mathbb{Z}$ under addition form a group: the operation is associative, $0$ is the identity, and every integer has an additive inverse. </example>
<lemma> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <lemma> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the lemma’s label, parallel to Theorem 2. ‘s name kwarg. Honored by the Phase-2 handler.
+numbered boolean default true Whether this lemma participates in the propositional theorem- family shared counter. Default true; -numbered suppresses.

Produced by: canonical <lemma>.

 Examples <lemma | Every continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum.> <lemma name="Zorn" #lem:zorn> Every non-empty partially-ordered set in which every chain has an upper bound contains a maximal element. </lemma>
<proof> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <proof> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix — e.g. “Proof (of Theorem 1.2)” or “Proof (sketch)”. Honored by the Phase-2 handler.
+numbered boolean default false Whether this proof is numbered. Default false — proofs are conventionally unnumbered (a proof’s identity comes from the theorem it proves, not from a counter). An author who wants numbering can opt-in per instance with +numbered.

Produced by: canonical <proof>.

 Examples <theorem | The sum of two even integers is even.> <proof> Let $a = 2m$ and $b = 2n$. Then $a + b = 2(m + n)$, which is even. $\square$ </proof>

The canonical pattern: <theorem> followed by sibling <proof>. The proof is NOT nested inside the theorem.

<proof name="of Theorem 1.2"> The argument follows from the preceding lemma. </proof>

Optional name kwarg lets the proof identify what it proves (useful when the proof is separated from its theorem by intervening text).

<proposition> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <proposition> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the proposition’s label.
+numbered boolean default true Whether this proposition participates in the propositional theorem-family shared counter. Default true.

Produced by: canonical <proposition>.

 Examples <proposition | The sum of two even integers is even.> <proposition name="Cauchy-Schwarz"> For any vectors $u$, $v$ in an inner-product space, $|\langle u, v \rangle| \le \|u\| \, \|v\|$. </proposition>
<remark> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <remark> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the remark’s label. Honored by the Phase-2 handler even though Remark. is unnumbered (a named remark may render as “Remark (Name):” without a number).
+numbered boolean default false Whether this remark is numbered. Default false — Remark. is conventionally unnumbered (the “remark” theorem-style family in amsthm is unnumbered). An author who wants numbering can opt-in per instance with +numbered, but most usage relies on the default.

Produced by: canonical <remark>.

 Examples <remark | The converse does not hold in general.> <remark> The hypothesis of compactness is essential here; without it the conclusion fails (consider $f(x) = 1/x$ on $(0, 1]$). </remark>
<theorem> Specification

category theorem-family · Layer 1 <theorem> · JATS <statement> · content prose → <children>

attribute kind values / default notes
name kwarg Optional name suffix for the theorem’s label (the “(Pythagoras)” half of “Theorem 1.2 (Pythagoras)”). Honored by the Phase-2 theorem handler at label-rendering time; until that handler lands, the kwarg flows through to the rendered HTML as data-name="..." via schema dispatch. LaTeX amsthm precedent: \begin{theorem}[Pythagoras].
+numbered boolean default true Whether this theorem participates in the theorem-family shared counter (see “Numbering” below). Use +numbered (default) to number; -numbered to suppress. Can also be written as numbered=true / numbered=false.

Produced by: canonical <theorem>.

 Examples <theorem | If $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ then the triangle is right-angled.>

Short-form with pipe content. The body is parsed normally.

<theorem name="Pythagoras" #thm:pyth> If $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$, the triangle with sides $a$, $b$, $c$ is right-angled. </theorem>

Long-form with the optional name kwarg. Cross-referenceable via id (the “thm:” colon-prefix convention is consistent with “fig:”, “eqn:”, “sec:” elsewhere in enscribe). The name kwarg lifts to data-name; the Phase-2 handler will render it as the “(Pythagoras)” suffix to the label “Theorem N”.
